name: Andini Maharani
bio: Andini leads product at Bayarin, a payments infrastructure company serving thousands of Indonesian merchants. Over twelve years she has shipped products across the full payments stack — from QRIS acceptance and disbursements to merchant lending.

Before Bayarin she scaled the payments platform of a major Indonesian e-commerce player from millions to tens of millions of monthly transactions, and she mentors early-career PMs through community programs.

showcase.title: Rebuilt merchant onboarding, activation up 38%
showcase.description: Led the end-to-end redesign of KYB onboarding, cutting median time-to-first-transaction from 6 days to 36 hours.

name: Bagas Prakoso
bio: Bagas runs the demand-side product group at Pasarin, an online marketplace connecting regional SME sellers with national buyers. His teams own search, discovery, and the buyer growth funnel.
He spent his earlier career in last-mile logistics, which still shows: he is happiest when a product decision can be argued with a cohort table and a unit-economics model.

showcase.title: Search relevance overhaul
showcase.description: Shipped a learning-to-rank search stack that lifted add-to-cart rate by 14% across long-tail queries.

name: Citra Ayudia
bio: Citra heads product at Sehatin, a healthtech startup making preventive care affordable for Indonesian families. She joined as the first product hire and built the team from zero to twelve.
Her specialty is taking fuzzy problem spaces from discovery to a launched v1 — she has done it four times across telemedicine, insurance, and wellness.

name: Dimas Pradipta
bio: Dimas owns the courier and routing platform at KirimKilat, the APIs and internal tools that move hundreds of thousands of parcels a day across the archipelago.
He writes a small newsletter about platform product management in Bahasa Indonesia and speaks regularly at local product meetups.

name: Eka Salsabila
bio: Eka builds AI products at Datain, where she leads the document-intelligence line used by banks and insurers to automate back-office workflows.
A former data analyst, she crossed over to product because she kept rewriting the specs anyway. She cares deeply about evals, latency budgets, and not shipping demos.

showcase.title: LLM document pipeline, 92% straight-through processing
showcase.description: Took claims-document extraction from OCR templates to an LLM pipeline with human-in-the-loop review, tripling throughput.

name: Fajar Ramadhan
bio: Fajar works on growth at Saku, a digital wallet for first-jobbers. He owns onboarding, referrals, and the experiments pipeline.
He started in management consulting, got bored of decks, and now A/B tests his way through the activation funnel.

name: Gita Larasati
bio: Gita leads the learner experience group at Bisa Academy, an upskilling platform with a stubborn focus on completion rates rather than enrollment numbers.
She previously built community products and brings that lens to education: cohorts, accountability, and social proof over content libraries.

name: Hendra Wijaksono
bio: Hendra is principal PM at Tumbuh, an HR and payroll platform for Indonesian SMEs. He owns the platform roadmap: APIs, integrations, and the partner ecosystem.
Twelve years in B2B taught him that enterprise products die by a thousand custom requests — his job, as he puts it, is saying no with a roadmap.

name: Intan Permatasari
bio: Intan builds the supply side of Liburin, a travel marketplace for local experiences. She works with thousands of small operators, from surf instructors in Canggu to batik workshops in Solo.
She is based in Bali and is a loud advocate for product careers outside Jakarta.

name: Jaka Saputra
bio: Jaka owns the underwriting product at Modalin, a productive-lending startup for warung and small retail. His day is split between credit models, OJK compliance, and field visits.
He believes the best fintech PMs in Indonesia are the ones who have sat in a warung at 6am watching how money actually moves.

name: Kirana Devi
bio: Kirana leads growth at Warungly, a bookkeeping and restocking app for micro-retailers. She works fully remote and runs a tight weekly experiment cadence with a three-person squad.
Her favorite growth lever is onboarding in Bahasa daerah — localized first-run experiences consistently beat any referral scheme she has tried.

name: Lukman Hakim
bio: Lukman is an APM at Ladang, an agritech startup digitizing the supply chain between smallholder farmers and modern retail. He owns the farmer-facing mobile app.
He joined from an APM program and spends two days a month in the field — his backlog is shaped more by farmer WhatsApp voice notes than by dashboards.
